summary: Henri Cartier-Bresson was a French humanist photographer and pioneer of street photography, known for his concept of the decisive moment. He co-founded Magnum Photos in 1947 and documented major events like Gandhi's funeral and the Chinese Civil War. He largely stopped photographing in the 1970s to focus on painting.

claims.evidence_quote: He was considered a master of candid photography, and was an early user of 35mm film.

claims.text: He pioneered the genre of street photography and viewed capturing what he named 'the decisive moment' as the essence of the very best pictures.
